title: Quantized affinity degradation and hosted backstop escape hatch
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Design and implement a controlled "quantized" affinity degradation strategy for dedicated capacity that reduces tenant affinity in deterministic steps, combined with a guarded "hosted backstop escape hatch" that limits and monitors hosted spillover during emergencies. Goal is to preserve SLOs for high-priority tenants while avoiding large-scale token storms or cache thrash when dedicated capacity becomes constrained.

Background and motivation:
- Current binary affinity demotion (dedicated -> hosted) causes sudden token bursts on hosted endpoints and large variations in latency/cost.
- We need a predictable, observable pathway to scale down dedicated routing for tenants with lower priority or who opted into resilience features.
- Operators require a fail-safe that can quickly evacuate traffic to hosted while preventing cascading failures and controlling financial exposure.

Proposed approach (high level):
1) Quantized Affinity Degradation: tenants have an affinity score represented as N discrete "lanes" (e.g., 4 lanes = 100%, 75%, 50%, 25%, 0%). On pressure signals (queue depth, slot scarcity, tail latency), we step tenants down one lane at a time with a hysteresis cooldown. Steps are time-bound and emitted as events so the console can show drift.
2) Token-budgeted Hosted Backstop Escape Hatch: instead of unlimited spillover, allocate a short-lived hosted token budget and per-tenant burst caps. When a tenant exceeds its budget, traffic is re-queued or demoted to lower-fidelity model variants. The escape hatch has a global circuit breaker and tenant-level soft-quarantine to prevent noisy neighbors.
3) Variant-aware fallback: when spilling to hosted, prefer quantized model variants that preserve API compatibility but are cheaper or smaller (quantized/8-bit variants). Runtime will map variant families and ensure structured output compatibility.
4) Observability and controls: expose metrics (affinity_lane, lane_transition_rate, escape_budget_used, host_spill_qps, variant_demote_count), add alerting for >10% global spillover sustained for 5m, and a console control to pin tenants to "no-spill" or "allow-escape".

Trade-offs and constraints:
- More granular lane state increases scheduler complexity and state machine transitions; requires careful optimization to avoid adding scheduling latency.
- Token budgets reduce immediate availability but prevent runaway spending; customers paying for Dedicated capacity might be surprised if budgeted spillover is used—need explicit billing docs.
- Variant demotion reduces model quality; must be tied to tenant SLAs and documented in rollout notes.

Acceptance criteria:
- Correct lane stepping under synthetic pressure load with hysteresis verified in unit+integration tests.
- Escape hatch enforces per-tenant and global budgets in chaos-testing (k-sim) with no more than 1% requests dropped under steady-state eviction scenarios.
- Console shows live affinity lane and budget consumption with per-tenant drilldown.
- End-to-end canary: 5% traffic for beta tenants for 24h with monitored rollback path.

Rollout plan:
- Feature flag behind runtime-config: quantized_affinity_v1.
- Internal canary (eng + infra tenants) for 1 week.
- Gradual expansion to customers who opt-in, default off for legacy tenants.

comments: 2025-09-03 — Triage: Added to routing-and-resilience project. Initial proposal reviewed by PM (Sofia Garber) who requested clearer customer opt-in flow.
2025-09-05 — Design sync: Agreed on 4-lane default and 10s minimum cooldown between steps. Action: Marcus to prototype lane state machine. (Design: Jeremy Holt)

2025-09-08 — Implementation note: Prototyped in routing-simulator; observed oscillation under bursty release patterns. Mitigation: add randomized backoff jitter to lane promotion and require 30s stable signal before promoting back up.
2025-09-10 — Ops feedback from incident INC-2025-07-14: learned that abrupt demotion caused cache invalidation storms — added escape token budget and tenant soft-quarantine to reduce cache churn.

2025-09-12 — PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/812 (prototype of quantized lane state + budget enforcement). Requesting review from @marcusliu and @susan-ng. Unit tests included.

2025-09-14 — Load test: 10k tenants simulated, global spillover capped at target budget; p99 latency on hosted remained within 1.6x baseline. Linked results above. Next: add regression tests for model-variant mapping compatibility.
2025-09-16 — Security review: scoped; no new surface for secrets. Confirmed no change to KMS interactions. Marking security_review_required=false but will include compliance note in customer docs.
2025-09-17 — PM review: Sofia approves canary parameters but asks for explicit billing note and opt-in wording before public rollout. Added follow-up task ENG-66700 for billing docs and legal review.
